item.title: No. 4 Ohio State hangs on to win at No. 5 Indiana, loses starting QB
item.description: Photo contributed by The Ohio State University (via website) The Ohio State University (via website) The No. 4 Ohio State Buckeyes hung on to beat the defending national champion Indiana Hoosiers on Saturday. The win may have come at a huge cost. [DOWNLOAD: Free WHIO-TV News app for alerts as news breaks ] The Buckeyes beat the Hoosiers, 19-15, in Bloomington, Indiana. But lost starting quarterback Julian Sayin to an injury in the fourth quarter. After the game, OSU head coach Ryan Day said that Sayin will “probably be out for several weeks,” as previously reported . TRENDING STORIES: Ohio State starting QB Julian Sayin expected to miss ‘multiple weeks,’ coach says 2 women who escaped Ohio corrections facility back in custody Can you help? Deputies looking for person of interest in counterfeit currency investigation Connor Hawkins made a 26-yard-field goal to give Ohio State a 3-0 lead. The Hoosiers took advantage of a Sayin interception in the second quarter. Turbo Richard’s seven-yard touchdown run put IU ahead, 7-3. The Buckeyes scored right before halftime. Sayin found Bo Jackson on fourth-and-goal for a two-yard touchdown, and OSU led 10-7 at the break. Ohio State recovered a fumble on the second play of the second half. It led to Hawkins’ second field goal, extending the lead to 13-7 after three. The Buckeyes faced a fourth down early in the fourth quarter. Sayin went deep to the end zone, and Jeremiah Smith caught it for a 38-yard touchdown. It expanded the lead to 19-7. Indiana answered with a 19-yard pass from Josh Hoover to Nick Marsh to cut the deficit to 19-15 with 10:30 left. Mario Landino sacked Sayin with 8:20 left, knocking the Buckeyes’ starting quarterback out of the game. Indiana faced a fourth-and-four from the Buckeyes’ 27-yard line with 1:07 left. Hoover threw to a wide-open Nick Marsh in the front corner of the end zone. The fireworks went off, but Marsh’s left foot stepped out of bounds. Video replays show that he put his hands on his helmet, knowing what happened. This was Indiana’s first home loss in Coach Curt Cignetti’s three seasons. It also snapped the Hoosiers’ 22-game winning streak. Sayin went 15-of-29 passes for 235 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions. Jeremiah Smith caught four passes for 68 yards and a touchdown. Ohio State enters the bye week with a 6-1 overall record and 4-0 in the Big Ten. The Buckeyes’ next game will be Oct. 31 at USC in Los Angeles. [SIGN UP: WHIO-TV Daily Headlines Newsletter ]

However, after Saturday’s 19-15 win over Indiana , it appears that Ryan Day and his offensive staff are going to have to figure out how to keep the Buckeyes’ national championship aspirations alive without their Heisman Trophy-finalist quarterback, at least for a little while. And even though true freshman Luke Fahey has clearly earned the coaching staff’s trust as Sayin’s primary backup, I can’t help but believe that Ohio State’s best chance to continue competing with the likes of USC, Oregon, and Michigan is to give sophomore Tavien St. Clair the opportunity to take over the offense. Now, I recognize that this probably sounds like the musings of an irrational fan caught up in the worry of the moment, but I think there is merit to it. Obviously, the coaches have watched considerably more of both quarterbacks than I have, and there is clearly a reason that Day and quarterbacks coach Billy Fessler have decided that Fahey deserves to be the first guy off the bench, and I’m certainly not suggesting that they made that decision arbitrarily. In August, Day said Fahey was “putting a lot of pressure on Tavien,” praising the freshman’s work ethic and ability to operate the offense. A month later, he explained that Fahey had earned the opportunity through his work in practice. That’s meaningful, and I don’t think it should be dismissed simply because St. Clair arrived in Columbus with considerably more recruiting hype. However, I also think there is a fundamental difference between the quarterback you trust to finish a game and the quarterback you trust to win the next five. If Sayin goes down in the middle of a close game, as he did on Saturday in Bloomington, you want someone who can immediately step into the huddle, understand the offense, make the right decisions, and avoid catastrophic mistakes. But when you have time to prepare a new starter, you have the opportunity to build an offense around what that quarterback does best, rather than simply asking him to execute the existing playbook. And when you have a bye week naturally built into that preparation process, I think you have to seriously consider which guy gives your offense the highest ceiling. And St. Clair has some pretty intriguing things that he does exceptionally well. At 6-foot-4 and 235 pounds, the former five-star prospect has five inches and nearly 30 pounds on Fahey (at least according to their official listings), along with the kind of arm strength that allows him to make throws all over the field. We saw glimpses of that potential during April’s spring game, when St. Clair completed 9 of 21 passes for 166 yards and a touchdown, including a gorgeous 40-yard scoring strike to Chris Henry Jr. He also connected with Henry on a beautifully placed 34-yard throw down the sideline, demonstrating the kind of downfield passing ability that could be particularly valuable with Jeremiah Smith lining up at receiver. In the spring game, St. Clair was 3-for-5 on deep balls for 112 yards and a touchdown, but struggled with intermediate throws, going just 2-for-8 on passes traveling between 10 and 20 yards downfield. Obviously, the 42.9% completion percentage is less than ideal; St. Clair missed plenty of throws, struggled with consistency, and made a couple of decisions that could have resulted in interceptions. He clearly still had work to do when it came to running the offense efficiently. Afterward, Day acknowledged both the talent and the growing pains, saying St. Clair needed to continue learning how to run the offense at a high level. And while he completed 5 of 6 passes for 52 yards and a touchdown against Ball State, we haven’t seen nearly enough of St. Clair in meaningful game situations this season to know how much progress he’s made since April. Clearly, it hasn’t been enough to cement the QB2 spot, and that uncertainty is the strongest argument against simply handing him the starting job. Of course, Ohio State fans don’t need to be reminded that a talented third-string quarterback who hasn’t quite put everything together can still accomplish some pretty remarkable things when given the opportunity. I’m certainly not suggesting that St. Clair is about to pull a Cardale Jones and lead the Buckeyes to a national championship, but if there’s one program that should understand the potential value of giving an unproven quarterback a chance to showcase his abilities, it’s this one. It’s not just recruiting pedigree or the memory of Cardale that has me intrigued by St. Clair’s potential. His physical advantages are real, too. On Saturday, we saw Fahey attempt a third-and-long dump-off to Legend Bey, only for the ball to hit the back of his own offensive lineman’s head. That’s certainly not a play that should define a freshman unexpectedly thrown into a top-five showdown, but it does illustrate how a quarterback’s size can affect his ability to see and deliver the ball through traffic. More importantly, St. Clair’s combination of size, arm talent, and mobility potentially gives Ohio State more ways to attack a defense than simply trying to replicate what Sayin has been doing since taking over the starting job. So, over the off week, I’d like to see Day, Arthur Smith, and Fessler make a serious effort to determine what St. Clair can comfortably execute against a legitimate Big Ten-caliber defense. Simplify the reads, incorporate quick throws, take advantage of his ability to stretch the field, and for the love of Woody Hayes, figure out how to establish a consistent running game. The Buckeyes don’t need St. Clair to become Julian Sayin overnight. They need him to get the ball to Jeremiah Smith, avoid putting the offense in impossible situations, and make enough plays to complement a defense that is finally beginning to look capable of carrying the team when necessary. There is risk in trusting a relatively inexperienced quarterback with that responsibility, especially one who hasn’t even been the primary backup, but with the schedule Ohio State has remaining, I think there is an even greater risk in limiting the offense’s potential simply because another quarterback has been better suited to the backup role. And if St. Clair isn’t able to demonstrate during the next two weeks that he’s ready for the responsibility, or if he gets his opportunity against USC and struggles, Fahey isn’t going anywhere. The Buckeyes would still have a quarterback the coaching staff clearly trusts to step in and run the offense. But with the luxury of an extra week to prepare, I think it would be a mistake not to at least explore whether St. Clair’s considerable physical gifts can translate into something serviceable, if not special, on Saturdays. If Sayin is going to miss significant time, as Day seemed to suggest in his postgame comments, the Buckeyes need more than someone who can simply keep the offense afloat. They need someone who gives them a chance to keep winning big games. And despite all the uncertainty, I believe St. Clair has the tools to be that guy.

item.title: Cross country: Exeter girls win invite, senior breaks 18-year record
item.description: WEST ROXBURY, Mass. — Exeter High School senior Lexi Paterna added another milestone to her cross country career on Saturday, Oct. 17 winning the Catholic Memorial Invitational and breaking a meet record that had stood since 2008. Paterna crossed the finish line in 17 minutes, 9 seconds, beating the previous course record of 17:17 set by Emily Jones of Bloomfield (Mass.) in 2008. Newton South's Isabelle Monaghan finished second in 17:58, and Exeter's Bri Paterna placed third in 18:08. Exeter also won the 21-team competition with 65 points. Needham (Mass.) was second at 133, and Oyster River was fifth (159). Exeter senior Izzie Bremer placed 10th overall in 18:40, giving the Blue Hawks three runners among the top 10. Ashleigh Maceachern added a 25th-place finish in 19:24, while Molly Kells completed Exeter's scoring five in 26th place at 19:29. Exeter's Lena McRae (28th, 19:37), Austin Williams (34th, 19:49) and Elliana York (35th, 19:52) all competed. Winnacunnet's Sofia Parisi was 27th (19:37), Oyster River junior Olivia Kavanagh placed 11th in 18:47, while senior Haley Bezanson was 21st (19:15). Other Oyster River runners included Madelyn Cook (29th, 19:43), Corina Sietz (51st, 20:26) and Drew Verweij (63rd, 20:48). Oyster River boys eighth, Exeter 10th Oyster River was paced by senior Oliver Lehman, who placed eighth overall in 15:48 seconds, and Levi Clapp finished 16th in 15:59. Brendan Banafato added a 44th-place finish in 16:38, while Ryker Andersen (63rd, 17:00) and Siddharth Sanjay (70th, 17:10) completed the team's scoring five. Oyster River totaled 201 points to place eighth out of 27 scoring teams. Exeter was led by senior Logen Poteet, who crossed the line 26th overall in 16:12. Colby Orleans finished 46th in 16:39, Henry Willett placed 61st in 16:59 and Xavier Garcia De Pare was 72nd in 17:12. Freshman Nolan Goldrick rounded out Exeter's scoring five with an 87th-place finish in 17:29. The Blue Hawks finished 10th in the team standings with 292 points. Exeter's Wyatt Maglin (17:30), Jackson Tooker (17:30), Noah Melendy (17:30), Alex Hodsdon (17:53) and Ryan Semesnyel (18:29) all competed. item.title: Gasperini: “I had no doubt we’d react this way.”
item.description: Gasperini: “I had no doubt we’d react this way.” Gian Piero Gasperini spoke to Sky Sport after Roma-Genoa (2-0). The Giallorossi coach commented on his team’s victory: “The first half wasn’t easy; it was difficult to measure Genoa. We had a very young team on the pitch, and they played well: we won a match that matters a lot.” The Grugliasco-born coach on the reaction after the Champions League defeat: “I had no doubts; in terms of character, the group is extraordinary. The match was still difficult, but we broke the deadlock with a fantastic play by Castro. Then the second half was valuable; in the first, we struggled with long balls to manage.” Gasperini on his growth since last season: “It wasn’t easy last year, I was just arriving. We’ve come a long way. Malen wasn’t there, Dybala was only occasionally present. Now we know more; 15-16 months have passed, and we’ve accumulated matches and successes. We made things difficult for ourselves in seven minutes with three corners that were the result of nothing. Real Madrid were struggling, and that bothered us. I had no doubts about our response despite the absences. I deliberately chose to make a lot of changes because many of the players had a lot of energy. Then we faced Genoa, who were causing us tactical problems. In the second half, we did well.”

item.title: Indiana WR Nick Marsh botching wide open TD catch vs. Ohio State has CFB world going insane
item.description: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images Indiana WR Nick Marsh botching wide open TD catch vs. Ohio State has CFB world going insane appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Indiana football earned the perfect opportunity to snatch the soul from Ohio State. OSU quarterback Julian Sayin exited on a sling. Then, IU wideout Nick Marsh caught a 27-yarder all alone in the end zone. Except officials ruled that end zone catch incomplete, creating a turnover on downs as IU faced a fourth-and-four. Why? Because Marsh’s foot stepped out of bounds, causing the refs to wave off the reception. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Josh Hoover finds Nick Marsh – BUT HE'S OUT OF BOUNDS pic.twitter.com/WCcs1mUefF — FOX College Football (@CFBONFOX) October 17, 2026 Ohio State, losers of the Big Ten title to this same Hoosiers team, escaped 19-15 in Bloomington. But Indiana’s 22-game winning streak officially died on the sidelines. The botched touchdown attempt fired off a flurry of social media reactions after the incomplete pass. “It feels like Ohio State has been on the receiving end of a lot of bad luck over the last few years. This time, the Buckeyes are the beneficiaries of some,” posted Ari Wasserman of On3 via the social media website X, formerly Twitter. “My goodness Ohio State got so dang lucky!” added host of The Pivot Podcast Ryan Clark. Andrew Jerrell Jones of the Bleav Network added a more unique take that would’ve perhaps prevented the incompletion. “If Curt Cignetti allowed Nick Marsh to wear gold cleats today, Marsh would have had a game winning TD and another incredible Cignetti-Indiana win over Ohio State,” Jones posted. Marsh would have finished with four receptions for 84 yards and two scores had the last touchdown counted. Indiana turned to Marsh to escape a possible meltdown against Nebraska just one week ago, scoring twice in under 12 minutes. But this time the Buckeyes grabbed the soul of the Hoosiers by inches. Oct 8, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago White Sox first baseman Munetaka Murakami (5) hits a single during the fifth inning against the Cleveland Guardians in game four of the ALDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Rate Field. Mandatory Credit: Matt Marton-Imagn Images ‎However, one of the major concerns for Murakami is his strikeout rate. He was struck out 196 times in the regular season, a 35.4% rate, just below his teammate Colson Montgomery with a 35.6% K rate (and 227 strikeouts). During the postseason, he struggled to hit fastballs below the belt, while his swing-and-miss was recurrent. He has been compared to Matt Olson and Kyle Schwarber , who are known big-hitters but have a high strikeout rate. The 26-year-old drew 92 walks, a 16.6% walk rate with a .347 OBP this year. ‎The Japanese slugger was originally acquired as a corner infielder, but he immediately blended into what the White Sox needed by playing primarily at first base or designated hitter. Despite playing a position he was not used to, Murakami registered a 2.3 WAR. But his Outs Above Average was zero, far below Montgomery’s +12 and Miguel Vargas’ seven. For a player learning a new position in the MLB, it is a completely neutral range score, and he can improve as he continues in the league. Does Murakami expect to be paid like one of the top first basemen in baseball? And are the White Sox comfortable making that type of financial commitment when they have other roster needs to address and legitimate concerns about his second-half performance? Chicago has plenty of legitimate reasons to believe that Murakami can be a cornerstone of their future, but they have to be careful about committing too much financial resources to a player who showed concerning weaknesses in the second half of the season. Oct 10, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Chicago White Sox first baseman Munetaka Murakami (5) reacts after striking out during the fourth inning against the Cleveland Guardians in game five of the ALDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Progressive Field. Mandatory Credit: David Richard-Imagn Images ‎The White Sox’s $34 million deal with Murakami served as a prove-it contract to establish his track record in the MLB, which he has done. His next deal will be a long-term one. First base players in their prime often get a seven-year contract extension of over $190 million or an eight-year contract of over $220 million. Murakami’s Average Annual Value (AAV) is between $25-$27 million a year, which he might accept, even though he will be eyeing to earn like the big boys in the league. However, a $180-$210 million, or seven-to-eight-year contract is likely to be the number for consideration, with a full no-trade clause and full opt-outs (year three). ‎Still, there’s a possibility that negotiations might not come together and Murakami will be in the final year of his contract next season. But White Sox would not want to put themselves in such a position, as his value will likely double and other big-money organizations like the New York Mets and New York Yankees will come for him. An agreement before spring training will be best for the White Sox and Murakami so that the focus will be on the season, and additional motivation to be successful will be locked in. And that can be done if both parties are serious about finalizing it early (or during the looming lockout). The houses are mostly built from that same generation. There are restaurants, bars, sidewalks and subdivisions. It’s a neighborhood. Like a Cubs game in Wrigleyville or a Notre Dame game in South Bend, there is a tangible aura as you pull into this town. I want that for the Bears. The Lombardi Trophy is everywhere – and I mean everywhere. I can see how they became “Entitledtown.” Of course, that would happen. item.title: Texas EDGE Colin Simmons suffered lower-leg injury vs. Florida
item.description: AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 17: Colin Simmons #1 of the Texas Longhorns is assisted to the sideline after an injury in the second half against the Florida Gators at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images AUSTIN — Texas Longhorns junior edge Colin Simmons suffered a lower-leg injury early in the fourth quarter of Saturday’s 27-24 loss to the Florida Gators on Saturday in Austin, head coach Steve Sarkisian said. Simmons was helped off the field before heading into the locker room on a cart. He did not return. “I don’t know the extent of it all,” Sarkisian said. 🚨 Texas EDGE Colin Simmons appears to sustain a right ankle injury. Can see his right foot forced into eversion and dorsiflexion, raising concern for a high ankle sprain involving the syndesmotic ligaments. pic.twitter.com/p4Wq5Lbv4p — Maddox McCloud, PT, DPT (@MaddoxMcCloudPT) October 17, 2026 The injury ended a superlative performance for the 6’3, 246-pounder, who recorded a sack to extend his national lead and finished with eight tackles (five solo), four tackles for loss, and two quarterback hurries. Colin Simmons with the feigned stab to ghost move. Dude is so fast, quick, and smooth working the arc. Lethal pass-rush threat. pic.twitter.com/sa8HkcI66K — Ian Cummings (@IC_Draft) October 17, 2026 Sarkisian also said that freshman running back Derrek Cooper did not receive a carry against the Gators because he wasn’t 100 percent. Cooper was not listed on any of the conference-mandated injury reports this week.

item.title: Pro Bodybuilding Mom, 40, Dies 2 Weeks After Taking Part in Fitness Competition
item.description: Marianne von Gierke Credit: Marianne von Gierke/Instagram NEED TO KNOW Marianne von Gierke, a 40-year-old Chilean bodybuilder, died on Wednesday, Oct. 14 Two weeks prior to her death, von Gierke finished in 13th place during the women’s physique category of a fitness competition “We will remember her for her dedication, discipline, and for taking her talent to the Mr. Olympia stage,” the Felipe Fierro Classic wrote in a tribute on Instagram A bodybuilder is dead just two weeks after competing in a fitness competition. She was 40. On Wednesday, Oct. 14, the Felipe Fierro Classic announced that Marianne von Gierke died. A spokesperson wrote on Instagram , “We will remember her for her dedication, discipline, and for taking her talent to the Mr. Olympia stage, leaving a legacy in her category and inspiring those who shared this passion with her.” They added of von Gierke, “Her effort, career, and all that she achieved will remain in the memory of our sports community.” “We send our deepest condolences to her family, loved ones, friends, and all those who mourn her passing,” the Felipe Fierro Classic spokesperson’s tribute continued. “We stand with you in respect and affection during this difficult time. May her legacy endure, and may she rest in peace.” Marianne von Gierke Credit: Marianne von Gierke/Instagram Two weeks before her death, von Gierke finished in 13th place in the women’s physique category of her latest competition, according to News.com.au . In 2024, she competed in the competition for the first time, when she finished in 16th place. Prior to competing, von Gierke earned the Women’s Physique crown at Rising Phoenix Arizona Pro in August, garnering a rare “perfect” judging scorecard of three points, per Argentine newspaper Clarin . Her victory granted her direct qualification into the latest competition. Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! The late athlete is survived by her 11-year-old son and her partner of 10 years, Juan Cofré García, Clarin reported. Marianne von Gierke Credit: Marianne von Gierke/Instagram In an Instagram tribute to her boyfriend three days before her death, von Gierke wrote, “Behind every competition, there’s also an effort that doesn’t appear in the photos: emotional support, psychological guidance, financial investment, shared decisions, and a life that often revolves around this sport.” “Thank you for believing in me, even when the road gets tough,” she continued. “For understanding this passion, experiencing it with me, and feeling every challenge as if it were yours too. Golden State's headline player is Gabby Williams, who has averaged an impressive 22.7 points per game in the playoffs so far. Along with Williams, the Valkyries will send out a strong defensive group with Veronica Burton and Kiah Stokes leading the charge. One viral claim about timing and manners pulled a famous German star into public debate. Practice courts rarely make headlines, even at the biggest events. Yet online fans quickly treated a rumor like a final verdict. That reaction says as much about social media habits as it does about tennis. What fans say happened on Court 5 A spectator posting on the Chinese social media platform RedNote claimed that Zverev had Court 5 booked for a practice session beginning at 10:30 a.m., but did not arrive until about 11:50 a.m. The post said Ben Shelton and 17-year-old Cruz Hewitt were scheduled to use Court 5 beginning at noon but were instead directed to Court 10 as Zverev began his practice. Those details came from spectator accounts and have not been independently confirmed by tournament organizers. Reports from spectators said Court 10 offered poorer viewing access, with some fans watching through a fence. The alleged switch prompted criticism online after the account spread across social media. Zverev laughs off the claims online Zverev defeated Quentin Halys 6-4, 6-7(8), 6-3 to advance at the Shanghai Masters and later responded to the practice-court allegations on social media. He wrote, “How do you even make stuff like this up?” followed by laughing emojis. Other reporting subsequently cited people who were present at the practice courts and said the interaction was less dramatic than some online posts suggested. Zverev himself denied the central allegations rather than acknowledging that he had improperly taken another player’s court time. Video from a brief practice-court interaction cannot establish every scheduling decision or conversation that took place behind the scenes. The available evidence therefore supports treating the original account as a disputed allegation rather than a confirmed finding. item.description: Gasperini: ‘No doubt Roma would respond, devastating loss to Real Madrid’ Gian Piero Gasperini ‘had no doubts’ Roma would react well to the Real Madrid match, as they beat Genoa 2-0. ‘Losing that way was devastating because the performance was so good.’ The Giallorossi were feeling the pressure after a run of disappointing results, including back-to-back Serie A draws with Inter and Como, but above all fumbling a 3-1 lead to lose 4-3 to Real Madrid here on Wednesday night. It took a while to break Daniele De Rossi’s Genoa down, but in the second half they came away with the points thanks to the first Roma goals from Santiago Castro and youth product Emanuele Lulli. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The No. 7 Texas Longhorns have lost two straight games after falling 27-24 to the Florida Gators in Week 7. It was another game in which the offense largely struggled, and now some of the fanbase is wondering if moving on from head coach Steve Sarkisian might be what’s best for the program. Texas ended the day with just 272 total yards of offense. The Longhorns only managed to record 13 first downs and went 2-10 on third-down conversions. Additionally, the program allowed five sacks, was forced to punt four times, and lost a fumble from quarterback Arch Manning (who went 173 yards and threw one touchdown with a 70.0% completion percentage) that allowed Florida to steal the win. The offense has been putrid this year, as it appeared to be difficult for Texas to move the ball down the field. Considering Sarkisian is the program’s playcaller, the fanbase hopped on social media, sharing their frustration with the 52-year-old. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Sark needs to go. Now,” one fan said . This user stated , “Oh, they lost. Sark needs to [be] fired today. All the resources in the world and he can’t coach for nothing.” “Fire Sark, bench Arch #hookem,” posted another upset fan . This individual claimed , “Sark on the hot seat.” “Do you think Sark even realizes he just lost to a backup QB on an unranked team at home while having one of the best rosters in the country?” Barstool Longhorns asked . Texas is scheduled to take on the Ole Miss Rebels, Mississippi State Bulldogs, Missouri Tigers, and LSU Tigers. item.title: Bath lose at home to Montpellier in Champions Cup
item.description: Donovan Taofifenua dived in at the corner to score the first of his two tries for Montpellier against Bath [Getty Images] Investec Champions Cup Bath (14) 14 Tries: Lawrence, Green Cons: Russell 2 Montpellier (10) 32 Tries: Hogg, Taofifenua 2, Becognee Cons: Hastings 3 Pens: Hastings 2 Montpellier earned an impressive victory at Bath, rounding off a disappointing Saturday for English clubs in the Champions Cup. After Gloucester's high-scoring draw against holders Bordeaux on Friday, Bath joined Sale, Bristol and Saracens in losing their opening pool fixture. Leicester, Exeter and Northampton are all in action on Sunday. Bath had scored at least 33 points in each of their first three Prem games this season but failed to reach those heights in attack during their Pool Four opener at The Rec. The hosts had a try disallowed in both halves, while Joe Cokanasiga failed to cleanly gather a pass with the tryline beckoning when they led 14-10 early in the second period. Bath were punished by Donovan Taofifenua's second-half double and an Alex Becognee try for last season's Challenge Cup winners Montpellier, who scored 22 points without reply after half-time. Recap: Saturday's Champions Cup action as it happened Bath had already had a Max Ojomoh try ruled out for a knock-on when Montpellier's former Scotland full-back Stuart Hogg raced in for the first points of the match. The hosts would soon be on the scoreboard themselves as England centre Ollie Lawrence barged over in the corner, before number eight Arthur Green brilliantly sidestepped past a defender to put the Prem club in front. Montpellier, beaten Top 14 finalists last season, kept in touch with an Adam Hastings penalty before the interval. Cokanasiga's missed opportunity proved costly almost immediately as winger Taofifenua dived over in the corner to make it 15-14 in the French side's favour. Hastings added a further three points from the tee and after an excellent defensive spell by the visitors, Taofifenua intercepted a Finn Russell pass on halfway and sped away from the chasing Bath defenders to score his second. Josh Bayliss' try for Bath did not stand because of an infringement earlier in the move, and Becognee burrowed over from close range in the final few minutes for Montpellier to make the win safe. Bath's remaining pool fixtures are against Cardiff, South African side Bulls and Stade Francais. The latter two of those teams met earlier on Saturday, with Bulls scoring eight tries in a convincing 56-20 victory against their French opponents. Cheswill Jooste ended with a hat-trick, having opened the scoring inside 20 seconds, in a bonus-point win. After Gloucester's high-scoring draw against holders Bordeaux on Friday, Bath joined Sale, Bristol and Saracens in losing their opening pool fixture. Leicester, Exeter and Northampton are all in action on Sunday. Bath had scored at least 33 points in each of their first three Prem games this season but failed to reach those heights in attack during their Pool Four opener at The Rec. The hosts had a try disallowed in both halves, while Joe Cokanasiga failed to cleanly gather a pass with the tryline beckoning when they led 14-10 early in the second period. Bath were punished by Donovan Taofifenua's second-half double and an Alex Becognee try for last season's Challenge Cup winners Montpellier, who scored 22 points without reply after half-time. Recap: Saturday's Champions Cup action as it happened Bath had already had a Max Ojomoh try ruled out for a knock-on when Montpellier's former Scotland full-back Stuart Hogg raced in for the first points of the match. The hosts would soon be on the scoreboard themselves as England centre Ollie Lawrence barged over in the corner, before number eight Arthur Green brilliantly sidestepped past a defender to put the Prem club in front. Montpellier, beaten Top 14 finalists last season, kept in touch with an Adam Hastings penalty before the interval. Cokanasiga's missed opportunity proved costly almost immediately as winger Taofifenua dived over in the corner to make it 15-14 in the French side's favour. Hastings added a further three points from the tee and after an excellent defensive spell by the visitors, Taofifenua intercepted a Finn Russell pass on halfway and sped away from the chasing Bath defenders to score his second. Josh Bayliss' try for Bath did not stand because of an infringement earlier in the move, and Becognee burrowed over from close range in the final few minutes for Montpellier to make the win safe. Bath's remaining pool fixtures are against Cardiff, South African side Bulls and Stade Francais. The latter two of those teams met earlier on Saturday, with Bulls scoring eight tries in a convincing 56-20 victory against their French opponents. Cheswill Jooste ended with a hat-trick, having opened the scoring inside 20 seconds, in a bonus-point win. item.title: 7 Eagles quarterback replacements after Jalen Hurts IR designation
item.description: The Philadelphia Eagles ‘ season is drastically shifting after the recent Jalen Hurts blood clot development. Philly’s star quarterback will now be sidelined indefinitely, which leaves the NFC East franchise with serious questions on offense. Hurts and the Eagles entered the 2026 NFL season with Super Bowl aspirations, just like their 2024 campaign. However, that playoff ambition is quickly changing and the franchise may have to scramble to find a long-term QB solution. Philadelphia luckily has options within their organization to survive in the short-term, but there’s always the possibility that the team looks outside the franchise as well. Who should the Eagles look to at quarterback until Hurts returns to action? Here are 7 QB options for the Eagles based on how the team approaches Hurts’ injury update, including four potential trade targets. However, if the Birds believe they can save their season then a move for someone of Jones’ capabilities would make sense. Last season, Jones threw for over 2,000 yards and 13 touchdowns for the Niners when stepping in for the injured Brock Purdy. Carson Wentz Wouldn’t that be quite the move for Philadelphia to bring Wentz back to the organization where he first started in the NFL? No matter how weird things got during his time with the team, Wentz is still a Super Bowl champion and had one of the greatest QB seasons in Eagles history before his injury in 2017. Mason Rudolph The Pittsburgh Steelers veteran has plenty of NFL experience, and that’s his biggest draw as a trade prospect. He’s not the most attractive name in the trade market, but the 31-year-old would be a cheap acquisition and could give the team enough to stay competitive in games. item.title: Castro: “I’m very happy with my first goal. My teammates and the staff gave me so much confidence.”
item.description: Castro: “I’m very happy with my first goal. My teammates and the staff gave me so much confidence.” Santaigo Castro scored his first goal for Roma against Genoa. Speaking to Sky Calcio, the Argentine striker commented on the match against the Ligurians, which ended 2-0 to the Giallorossi. Regarding the impact of his first goal for the Giallorossi, Castro said: “I’m very happy; it’s so important. Today was a very tough match because we knew they play man-to-man. Daniele knows how to play against us, and last year, at their home, it was also a difficult match. We managed to score early in the second half and then played well, creating chances. We’re happy because today, players who haven’t played much so far got a lot of minutes.” “Even the players who missed today’s match and the staff gave us confidence. They’re extraordinary guys. I’m three years older than him, but he works like a dog, runs, runs, runs, and learns every day, like all the guys. He deserves it so much; he’s a golden boy.” “I hit a lot of posts, but I worked hard. The guys, not just the staff, but also the Argentinians and everyone else, gave me so much confidence. This is important, not just for me, but for everyone, because, as I said before, many guys who hadn’t had many minutes played today. And all the starters—so to speak, because no one feels like a starter or part of a second team—gave us so much confidence. We managed to win this difficult match and stay where we wanted to be,” Castro concluded.

item.title: Texas A&M bounces back, rides rushing attack to blowout of The Citadel
item.description: Jamarion Morrow scored three touchdowns as Texas A&M cruised past The Citadel on Saturday in College Station. (Adam Davis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) COLLEGE STATION - Texas A&M returned to the win column Saturday with a 41-0 victory over The Citadel in a ground-and-pound contest highlighted by three touchdowns from Jamarion Morrow. The Bulldogs (2-5) entered running the ball about 73% of the time while the Aggies (4-3) focused on their rushing attack against the FCS opponent. The result was a first half where 46 of 62 combined plays between the teams were rushing attempts. Each team might have been trying to establish the run but only Texas A&M could turn it into points. The Aggies were up 28-0 at the half with nearly 200 more total yards gained despite having the ball for only 11 minutes. Four different Texas A&M players accumulated 148 rushing yards in the first half with Morrow finding the end zone three times. He's the first player with three rushing touchdowns in a game since Le'Veon Moss last year against Notre Dame. The Aggies finished with a season-high 263 rushing yards. Freshman KJ Edwards led the way with 116 yards on 13 carries, including two 30-plus-yard runs. Marcel Reed, who only played the first half, also found Aaron Gregory on a play-action pass for a 37-yard touchdown. He had 130 passing yards and another 23 yards on the ground. Backup quarterback Brady Hart was 8 of 12 for 107 yards and a touchdown. The Aggies were without five typical starters, including wide receivers Mario Craver and Ashton Bethel-Roman. item.title: Packers place 3 on injured reserve before Week 6 vs. the Cowboys
item.description: (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers announced a flurry of moves on Saturday as the team tries to get their roster in order for their Sunday Night Football matchup against the Dallas Cowboys. The Packers are dealing with several injuries, which led to four players being ruled out on Friday , forcing Green Bay to push up some reinforcements. The Packers placed defensive lineman Jonathan Ford, defensive lineman Javon Hargrave and wide receiver Skyy Moore on the injured reserve today. Those were three of the four players who were already ruled out against the Cowboys, with the non-IR’d player being cornerback Benjamin St-Juste. Backfilling on the game-day roster are receiver Savion Williams, who was activated from the injured reserve on Saturday, and elevated practice squadders Arron Mosby (edge) and Coleman Owen (receiver). Below is a full breakdown of the Packers’ position groups heading into the game, including their injury statuses. Quarterback Jordan Love Tyrod Taylor Running Back MarShawn Lloyd Pierre Strong Jr. Kaleb Johnson Receiver Christian Watson Matthew Golden Bo Melton Savion Williams (questionable) J. Michael Sturdivant Coleman Owen Tight End Tucker Kraft Mark Redman Jonnu Smith Josh Whyle Offensive Line Jordan Morgan Laken Tomlinson Sean Rhyan Travis Glover Anthony Belton Kevin Zeitler Aaron Banks (questionable) Jacob Monk (questionable) Donovan Jennings Jager Burton John Williams Defensive Line Karl Brooks Devonte Wyatt Chris McClellan Anthony Campbell (questionable) Edge Defender Lukas Van Ness Barryn Sorrell Brenton Cox Jr. Dani Dennis-Sutton Arron Mosby Linebacker Zaire Franklin Isaiah McDuffie Ty’Ron Hopper Nick Niemann Kristian Welch Cornerback Keisean Nixon Brandon Cisse (questionable) Carrington Valentine Benjamin St-Juste (out) Kamal Hadden Safety Xavier McKinney Evan Williams Javon Bullard Kitan Oladapo Specialist Trey Smack (K) Daniel Whelan (P) Matt Orzech (LS) With St-Juste already ruled out, the Packers have 51 options to make up their 48-man roster. In all likelihood, the team will scratch 3 of their 11 offensive linemen, since it’s very rare for NFL teams to carry more than 8 at the position into a game. It seems like the team believes that all of the players with questionable statuses will play on Sunday, and even then they’re really short at some positions. For example, they have one backup defensive lineman for their 3-4 defensive front, and that’s if Anthony Campbell (listed as questionable) is able to play. In the secondary, they have just eight players total at cornerback and safety, and that’s if rookie Brandon Cisse (questionable) can go. The defense isn’t going to have many options, which is an interesting decision for the team to make going into a matchup against the best offense they’ve seen this season.

item.title: Jalen Hurts injury takes a scary shift as Eagles move him to injured reserve
item.description: Jalen Hurts injury takes a scary shift as Eagles move him to injured reserve originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Last week, the Philadelphia Eagles announced that star quarterback Jalen Hurts wouldn't be playing in Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers due to a blood clot. However, it seemed to be a one-and-done kind of deal, and there wasn't any mention of him being out for a very long time. That's changed, though, and the Eagles announced on Saturday that they're placing Hurts on injured reserve. The team shared the news in a post on X, stating that Hurts would be on the injured reserve list and that it was also signing running back Jaydon Blue to the active roster. They're also elevating Keyshawn James-Newby and Cole Wisniewski for the upcoming game. Earlier on Saturday, ESPN reported that the team had "not even discussed the possibility of injured reserve," so this is quite a turn of events. Jalen Hurts' injured reserve placement raises questions about when the Philadelphia Eagles quarterback could return from his blood clot Up next, the Eagles take on the Panthers, followed by the Dallas Cowboys , Washington Commanders and New York Giants . item.title: Elandon Roberts’ Steelers Return Will Wait another Week
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers inside linebacker Elandon Roberts during a game against the Buffalo Bill son Aug. 27, 2026. -- Ed Thompson /. Steelers now The Pittsburgh Steelers faithful will have to wait at least one more week for the return of popular inside linebacker Elandon Roberts. Roberts was not elevated from the Steelers’ practice squad by the Steelers before Saturday’s deadline, meaning he will not be eligible to play in Week 6, when the Black and Gold visit the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. The Steelers called up three others from the practice squad, signing running back Lew Nichols and elevating wide receivers Brandon Johnson and Brandon Smith as the club deals with a slew of injuries at offensive skill positions. Wide receivers Michael Pittman Jr., Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek have all already been ruled out against the Buccaneers, while tight end Pat Freiermuth and running back Rico Dowdle are questionable. Roberts re-joined the Steelers via the practice squad on Monday. The 32-year-old had been one of the team’s final cuts coming out of training camp. Pittsburgh Steelers inside linebacker Elandon Roberts during a game against the New York Jets on Oct. 21, 2024. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Roberts was with the Steelers from 2023-24, and then spent last season with the Las Vegas Raiders, where he played for current Steelers defensive coordinator Patrick Graham . He rejoined the team this summer, late in training camp, “I enjoyed him in training camp,” head coach Mike McCarthy said on Monday. “I thought he did a nice job. I think timing was a little bit to do with his opportunity. Once again, we’re trying to get better. All these opportunities that we are creating for players. The changes that you make, we’re trying to improve the team. He’s a veteran. He’s done great things throughout his career, but this man just wants to win. Can’t have enough people like that.” The Steelers do not have any injuries or obvious need for an additional linebacker to dress. Starters Patrick Queen and Payton Wilson and backups Carson Bruener and Cole Holcomb have been active in all five games so far this season. item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. item.title: Christian Pulisic is no longer a focal point for the US or Milan – and that’s OK
item.description: The winger is 28, and younger teammates are rising into the high-pressure spots he has usually occupied Usually, the second weekend of October sees Christian Pulisic flanked by compatriots as the Star-Spangled Banner plays. Last year, he was involved in US friendlies against Ecuador and Australia. But this year, with Fifa having folded the October window into September, Pulisic didn’t have the chance. On Sunday, his pre-match music was O Generosa, the Serie A anthem, which he observed with a soft smile. Mark Twain’s first visit to Italy left him describing the country as “a vast museum of magnificence and misery”, and it’s a fitting summary of Pulisic’s three-plus years with Milan. item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. The majority of people involved in the game speak it with a high degree of sophistication. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. Those gleefully wielding inflatable bananas in the Anfield away end could thumb their noses. Why not enjoy the dances of defiance until the music stops? The same went for City players, asked to perform under the darkest of clouds, able to focus, at last, on football, rather than legal argument and uncertain futures. Beyond City, the sight of a club found guilty of 100-plus charges laying waste to such rivals as Liverpool was deeply uncomfortable . The Premier League season and product are badly damaged until the matter is somehow resolved. What happened at Anfield should double the haste for a resolution. Chants of “cheat” whenever City players, the game already won, slipped the ball around, are bound to be repeated at other stadiums. Enzo Maresca has described his club’s plight as “noise” but his team’s victory did absolutely nothing to turn the volume down. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
